Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From ee66bc29578391c9b48523dc9119af67bd5c7c0f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Vinicius Costa Gomes <vinicius.gomes@intel.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 10:34:36 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] dmaengine: idxd: Fix leaking event log memory

During the device remove process, the device is reset, causing the
configuration registers to go back to their default state, which is
zero. As the driver is checking if the event log support was enabled
before deallocating, it will fail if a reset happened before.

Do not check if the support was enabled, the check for 'idxd->evl'
being valid (only allocated if the HW capability is available) is
enough.

Fixes: 244da66cda35 ("dmaengine: idxd: setup event log configuration")
Reviewed-by: Dave Jiang <dave.jiang@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Vinicius Costa Gomes <vinicius.gomes@intel.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260121-idxd-fix-flr-on-kernel-queues-v3-v3-10-7ed70658a9d1@intel.com
Signed-off-by: Vinod Koul <vkoul@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/dma/idxd/device.c b/drivers/dma/idxd/device.c
index efd7bfccc51f..131138483b87 100644
--- a/drivers/dma/idxd/device.c
+++ b/drivers/dma/idxd/device.c
@@ -834,10 +834,6 @@ static void idxd_device_evl_free(struct idxd_device *idxd)
 	if (!evl)
 		return;
 
-	gencfg.bits = ioread32(idxd->reg_base + IDXD_GENCFG_OFFSET);
-	if (!gencfg.evl_en)
-		return;
-
 	mutex_lock(&evl->lock);
 	gencfg.evl_en = 0;
 	iowrite32(gencfg.bits, idxd->reg_base + IDXD_GENCFG_OFFSET);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file (`drivers/dma/idxd/device.c`) to fix a memory leak in the event log cleanup during device removal. The change removes two lines that checked the hardware register `IDXD_GENCFG_OFFSET` to see if the event log was enabled before deallocating. This check was problematic because the device reset (e.g., during remove) restores the register to its default (zero), causing the check to fail and skip freeing the event log memory. The fix ensures that deallocation is performed whenever the event log structure (`idxd->evl`) exists, regardless of the register state. The relationship between the modifications is that the removal of the register read and early return allows the subsequent cleanup code to execute unconditionally when the event log has been allocated, thus preventing the memory leak.

1. The root cause.
2. Code statements that lead to the bug and the reason for it.

Think step by step.

Root cause:
During device removal, the device reset clears the event log enable bit in the hardware register (IDXD_GENCFG_OFFSET), causing the `idxd_device_evl_free()` function to incorrectly skip deallocation of the event log memory, resulting in a memory leak.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
gencfg.bits = ioread32(idxd->reg_base + IDXD_GENCFG_OFFSET);
if (!gencfg.evl_en)
    return;
Reason:
During device removal, a hardware reset clears the event log enable bit (`gencfg.evl_en`). The above check then causes `idxd_device_evl_free()` to return early without freeing the previously allocated event log memory, leading to a memory leak.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
if (!evl)
    return;
// (the two lines reading and checking gencfg are removed)
Reason:
The fix removes the hardware register check. Instead, it relies solely on the `evl` pointer (which is only non-NULL if the event log was allocated). This ensures that deallocation always occurs when memory was previously allocated, regardless of the hardware register state after a reset.


Now, determine whether the provided code snippet is buggy:

	mutex_lock(&evl->lock);
	gencfg.evl_en = 0;

Result: <yes or no>

Result: no
